name: countdown-slot
description: Start a 1P game whose life-start seat (sequence arm 3, 0x4C75) loads era 3 (1983) from the player's own saved-era cell, then trigger fire bursts until a player shot destroys an object in the era-2+ object bank; the struck slot takes a countdown marker and the era-2+ sweep runs its drifting-countdown arm, stepCountdownSlotThenCloseTurn (0x4108). Whether that object is debris or an explosion is not settled (names.js 0x4108).
_grounding: 0xAD14 is PLAYER_ONE_ERA_INDEX (the player's saved era, copied into play at every life start), poked to 3 before the life-start arms run; 0xAA81 is SHOT_BURST_PENDING, poked every 16 frames to fire bursts. In the JS engine the first countdown marker (0xF0) lands in slot 0xA8C0 from destroyTargetsHitByShots (0x5211). 'responded' 0xAA58 eq 0x0D is the SPRITE_STATE byte (iy+0x30) of that slot's sprite entry, and 0x0D is the arm's NEAR_STATE: statically, the ROM's only store of 0x0D to (iy+0x30) is `ld (iy+0x30),0x0d` at 0x4169 (translated/loc_413c.js), inside 0x413C, whose only caller is the `call 0x413c` at 0x4108 (byte scan of maincpu.bin); per independent static review, the other (iy+0x30) writers cannot produce 0x0D at 0xAA58 in era 3. So the golden responding on frames 1001..1550 means MAME itself ran the arm. Reach counts: oracle = calls (routine-map dispatch); idiomatic = probe reads of the slot's countdown byte, two per call.
_distant_budget_px: 16px, measured against MAME: the correct layers' distant-state floor is 0px (oracle) and 2px (idiomatic), band 0px on both. At the default budgets two arm mutants PASSED (idiomatic vs MAME): NEAR_STATE 0x0d->0x02 (distant max 87px, band worst 87px) and the arm with both sprite-entry writes removed (distant max 90px, band worst 89px). With 16px both FAIL, on the distant-state window and on the band (27 consecutive over-budget band frames each).
